channel.title: Middle East AI Monitor
channel.description: AI monitoring of Israel/Gaza, Iran, Syria, Lebanon and Iraq developments

item.title: Hamas official's arrest in Gaza gave Israel intelligence surge to kill top terrorists - exclusive
item.description: Three Hamas brigade commanders have been killed since September 11, following the September 2 capture of senior Hamas security official Mu'in al-Arabid in Gaza.

item.title: Israel revokes aliyah approval for Jewish activists involved in pro-Palestinian advocacy
item.description: The Population and Immigration Authority overturned the aliyah approvals of two activists in their 20s, who have worked with Palestinian communities in the West Bank.

item.title: Netanyahu falls back on classic security playbook as election approaches - analysis
item.description: "Netanyahu does not surrender" is the official slogan for Netanyahu's right-wing Likud party, which most opinion polls predict will lose around a third of its parliamentary seats.

item.title: WATCH: IDF strikes in Gaza, killing Hamas Northern Brigade commander, top military financer
item.description: Beik had served as commander of the brigade since the elimination of his predecessor, Ahmed Ghandour, and had previously served as the brigade’s military intelligence chief, according to the IDF.

item.title: Tensions spike as Israel targets Dutch diplomats following Netherlands ban on settlement goods
item.description: The change in Dutch policy has not eliminated domestic disagreements. Criticism has been voiced even within D66, with some arguing that the government is not putting sufficient pressure on Israel

item.title: Iranian students protest compulsory hijab, university costs as campus unrest returns
item.description: Iranian university students protested against compulsory hijab and worsening economic conditions, with Basij forces accused of threatening demonstrators during the campus gathering.

item.title: Iranians stagger under soaring cost of living after seven months of war with the US
item.description: How far economic strain may push Iran towards diplomatic compromise is unclear, as it tightens its own stranglehold on Gulf energy exports through the Strait of Hormuz, driving up oil and gas prices.

item.title: Over 100 Jewish extremist settlers riot near West Bank town, clash with Israeli forces
item.description: Three Border Police officers lightly wounded as extremist settlers clash with forces, setting fire to Palestinian property • Riot sought to prevent Palestinian family’s coordinated return to Jalud

item.title: Iran's Islamic regime using Tether cryptocurrency as 'financial lifeline,' US Senate report charges
item.description: The report ⁠found that 84% of crypto wallets that have been sanctioned by the US transacted in USDT, such as to help ​the Iranian government move money across its borders and support ​its currency.

item.title: No. 1: Jared Kushner and Ivanka Trump: Remembering who brought the hostages home
item.description: Jared Kushner and Ivanka Trump helped achieve what few in Jerusalem thought possible, bringing every Israeli hostage home and reshaping the Middle East.

item.title: No. 3: Gadi Eisenkot: Israel’s next prime minister?
item.description: The former IDF chief has emerged as the leading opposition challenger to Netanyahu, offering voters a path to a post-Netanyahu Israel.

item.title: No. 4: Naftali Bennett: The former PM seeking a comeback to ‘repair Israel’
item.description: Since returning to politics, Bennett has shifted from his previous campaigns, taking a more liberal position while maintaining a strong right-wing stance on security.

item.title: No. 5: Ronald Lauder: Standing at the forefront of the fight against antisemitism
item.description: Lauder has never confined himself to quiet philanthropy - he continues to use his position to demand accountability from political leaders.

item.title: No. 2: Benjamin Netanyahu: Shaping Israel’s politics and global image for a generation
item.description: Netanyahu has become more than Israel’s prime minister for many. Abroad, for instance, he has become Israel’s symbol and the lightning rod for much of the hatred directed against the Jewish state.

item.title: Netanyahu condemns riots in West Bank, calls to fully prosecute extremist settlers involved
item.description: Settler extremists threw stones, assaulted IDF and Border Police, and set fire to property throughout the area, actions which members of the establishment utterly condemned.

item.title: Fmr. defense minister Gallant confirms additional details of Mossad's Hezbollah pager operation
item.description: Many of the details mentioned by Gallant in the interview were previously reported by The Jerusalem Post during an interview with Mossad agent "Adam Feyn" in May.

item.title: Ex-Shin Bet chief threatens defamation suit against Netanyahu amid 'unrestrained incitement'
item.description: Bar is also demanding the disclosure of Netanyahu's schedule of meetings with the defense establishment and foreign officials. He said he intends to summon members of the prime minister's office.

item.title: PMO: Shin Bet files complaint to IDF censor after Channel 12 report 'endangered' Netanyahu's life
item.description: The Shin Bet said the timing of Channel 12's report on Netanyahu's flight to the UAE "endangered the security of the prime minister, the operation, and the forces on the ground."

item.title: Rubio’s Israel stance would change the moment he ran for president, Vance ally Hazony claims
item.description: Yoram Hazony, a founder of the national conservatism movement, says Republicans risk losing the White House if they alienate Tucker Carlson’s supporters.

item.title: Russia opposes Iran leaving nuclear non-proliferation treaty, Kremlin says
item.description: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov was responding to comments from Iranian officials about Tehran's possible withdrawal from the treaty, which commits Tehran not to develop or acquire nuclear weapons.
